content: The ZZZ3 protein, which contains a zinc finger domain, is encoded by the ZZZ3 gene in humans. To investigate the function of ZZZ3, model organisms have been utilized. Specifically, a conditional knockout mouse line, named Zzz3tm1a(EUCOMM)Wtsi, was created as part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program. This program is a large-scale mutagenesis initiative designed to produce and distribute animal models of human diseases to researchers worldwide. Both male and female mice from this knockout line underwent a standardized phenotypic screening process to assess the effects of the gene deletion. A total of 24 tests were conducted on the mutant mice, and two significant abnormalities were identified. No homozygous mutant embryos were detected during gestation, and none survived to the weaning stage, indicating embryonic lethality in homozygous mutants. The remaining tests were performed on heterozygous mutant adult mice, and no additional abnormal phenotypes were observed in these animals.
